definition.text: Runtime/Sandbox is the boundary one unit of agent work runs inside. This repo's own target architecture states the requirement directly and names the standard it is checked against: "a unit of work runs isolated, per the OCI Runtime Spec" -- satisfied today by a Firecracker microVM per unit of work.

evidence.quote: a unit of work runs isolated, per the OCI Runtime Spec

standards.role: governs the boundary itself: the lifecycle and configuration interface every isolation adapter (a plain process, Docker, gVisor, Kata, Firecracker) must implement so callers see one declare/admit/inspect contract regardless of which adapter is behind it.
standards.covers: does not say anything about what is inside the sandbox (base image, toolchain, dependency versions) -- that is the Image Spec's job, not the Runtime Spec's.

evidence.text: The OCI Runtime Spec defines the behavior and the configuration interface of low-level container runtimes such as runc.

evidence.quote: The OCI Runtime Spec defines the behavior and the configuration interface of low-level container runtimes such as runc.
status (string, REQUIRED) is the runtime state of the container.

standards.role: governs the contents half: the image manifest, content-addressable filesystem layers, and image config that get unpacked into the OCI Runtime Bundle the Runtime Spec already governs.
standards.covers: packaging and distribution/addressing only -- it does not select a toolchain, decide a caching policy, or provide reuse across many agent runs; current release is v1.1.1 (March 2025), older than this pass's recency preference but cited as the canonical spec itself.

evidence.text: The goal of this specification is to enable the creation of interoperable tools for building, transporting, and preparing a container image to run.

evidence.quote: The goal of this specification is to enable the creation of interoperable tools for building, transporting, and preparing a container image to run.

landscape.text: The real, measured tradeoff in how much a sandbox's declared contents cost is not storage, it is startup latency: "Dependency size has a measurable effect on cold start latency on many serverless platforms. Larger payloads drive longer initialization windows." Current production practice answers this with pre-warmed memory/filesystem snapshotting rather than image shrinking alone. Separately, no single convention governs how an agent's environment contents are declared in the first place: devcontainer.json, hand-written Dockerfiles, and Nix flakes are all in concurrent, unreconciled use across different agent CLIs as of mid-2026.

evidence.quote: Dependency size has a measurable effect on cold start latency on many serverless platforms. Larger payloads drive longer initialization windows.
Dev Containers (devcontainer.json) — VS Code spec; used by trailofbits/claude-code-devcontainer.
Nix solves the complementary problem: ensuring the agent has a consistent, complete set of tools to work with.

usage.text: This repo's own planning layer treats isolation as one of several smart-defaulted concerns the caller does not configure directly: the mechanism exists specifically to remove the need to "decide routing, isolation, retries, model tier, budget ceiling, deadline, telemetry, provenance, the ledger" -- a caller writes `intent:`, and one word of `profile:` only if the default bundle picked for it is wrong.

evidence.quote: decide routing, isolation, retries, model tier, budget ceiling, deadline, telemetry, provenance, the ledger

gaps.what: No named standard declares an agent's environment contents end to end (base image, toolchain, exact dependency versions); only fragmented point solutions exist today (devcontainer.json, hand-written Dockerfiles, Nix flakes, Kubernetes SandboxTemplate).
gaps.why_it_matters: Without one, reproducibility and caching policy for the contents half of the sandbox is reinvented per agent CLI, and this repo has not picked one either.
gaps.research_query: is there a 2027+ convergence candidate for declaring agent-sandbox environment contents beyond OCI Image Spec

gaps.what: The split between a cacheable, warm-pool environment template and the per-run sandbox claim/bind step -- already implemented by Kubernetes SIG Agent Sandbox's SandboxTemplate resource -- is not built in this repo's own cap-isolation.
gaps.why_it_matters: Without the split, every sandbox likely pays the full cold-start cost this card's own evidence shows is dominated by dependency/image size, rather than amortizing it across a warm pool.
gaps.research_query: does this repo's cap-isolation harness distinguish an environment template resource from a sandbox claim

gaps.what: Every harness's live adapter, Firecracker included, is claimed rather than measured against a real host from a session (per STATUS row 37) -- so the 'built' status on this card rests on unverified claims for the live path.
gaps.why_it_matters: A capability marked 'built' whose live adapter has never run is a different risk than one that has been measured.
gaps.research_query: has any harness run its live adapter against a real host and recorded the result
